raw_response:
I have been growing cotton here for 30 years. I do what works. Last year I got maybe 280 kg per mu, that was okay. I will do about the same this year.

For seed, I buy from the same dealer in town. He sells the good kind, the one that resists the worm — everyone around me plants it, so I plant it too. I do not know the name, I just ask for what my neighbor Old Wang buys.

For fertilizer, I use what I always use. I put down two bags of compound fertilizer per mu before planting — that is about 50 kg, and then I top-dress with urea when the cotton starts flowering, maybe one bag per mu. My neighbor uses a little less but his field is worse than mine. I would rather put a bit extra than see my bolls drop. Fertilizer costs money but losing the harvest costs more.

I plough the field before planting, that is how we always do it here. Rotary is for those who rent machines, I use my own plough.

Water — I have a well, thank heaven. I water maybe 3 times: once after sowing to help it come up, once when it flowers, once when bolls are filling. If the summer is dry I water more.

Pesticides — cotton is the worst for bugs. Even with the good seed, I still spray for aphids, mites, and the boll worms that come later. Maybe 10 times through the season. I spray when I see the bugs, or when Old Wang sprays.

My field is 12 mu, it is just me and my wife. Cotton is hard work but the price this year should be okay.
